transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Jared Cole (Head of Product, OmniHealth); Maya Rivera (Security & Privacy Lead, OmniHealth); Dr. Sanjay Patel (ML Engineer, OmniHealth)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, im alex from Redwood, priya is our solutions engineer. thanks for the time.
[00:12] Jared Cole: thanks alex. we only got 50 minutes so want to focus on data handling for the POC — pii, retention, logging, that kind of stuff.
[00:20] Priya Singh: yeah totally. our goal today is to scope the POC around your data constraints, benchmark goals, and timeline. i have a draft plan to walk through.
[00:30] Maya Rivera: hi all. my main ask is we cannot have raw patient identifiers logged anywhere. we need redaction, kms encryption, and an option for private deploy if hosted is a no-go.
[00:42] Alex Kim: totally understood. quick question on scope — is the POC using synthetic data or a sampled subset of real data?
[00:50] Dr. Sanjay Patel: plan is to use a deidentified subset first, but we will need a follow-up run with near-production data (PHI-like) to validate redaction and latency. that will require strict access controls.
[01:05] Priya Singh: ok good. two tracks: 1) benchmark synthetic/deid dataset to validate latency and throughput, 2) validate redaction + retention settings on a locked-down environment.
[01:18] Jared Cole: success criteria — we want 95th percentile latency under 350ms for our typical prompt size, sustained throughput of ~40 qps during peak simulation, and cost to be under $0.02 per 1k tokens — we know cost target is approximate.
[01:35] Priya Singh: noted. benchmarking team will measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost; we can run both hosted and dedicated profiles to compare.
[01:45] Maya Rivera: on retention — we need confirmation that prompts and completions containing PII are not stored beyond X days. our initial ask is max 30 days for logs and ability to opt-out for any data stored for model tuning.
[01:58] Alex Kim: Redwood supports configurable retention settings per-customer in the control plane. for hosted we have retention windows and an option to disable retention entirely for PII fields — with caveat that certain telemetry for SLA reasons may be kept in masked form.
[02:15] Dr. Sanjay Patel: how does that masking work? is it automatic or do we have to provide patterns?
[02:21] Priya Singh: we offer a few approaches: client-side redaction before sending, server-side automatic redaction we can configure using regex/field maps, and an SDK hook to sanitize prompts. for the POC we can do both to verify.
[02:36] Jared Cole: client-side redaction is preferable but we'd like to test server-side in case devs accidentally send raw identifiers. also want to log a redaction audit trail.
[02:48] Maya Rivera: audit trail is essential. we need to see what was redacted (hash only, never raw values), who triggered, timestamp, and the rule matched.
[02:58] Priya Singh: audit logs can include redaction tags and hash fingerprints. we don't store raw values in the logs; we can show matching rule ids and salted hashes for traceability.
[03:10] Alex Kim: on encryption — all data in transit and at rest is encrypted. we support customer-managed keys via KMS for private deployments and dedicated customers; hosted customers can also opt into CMK with additional compliance steps.
[03:24] Maya Rivera: good. do you integrate with Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS?
[03:29] Priya Singh: yes — AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault supported for CMK. we also have HSM options for Private deployments.
[03:36] Jared Cole: prompt storage concerns — do you persist prompts to improve the model by default?
[03:41] Alex Kim: no, not by default. hosted environment has a retention/consent model — data is used for service improvement only with explicit consent; for POC we'll disable any model training and set retention to your policy. Dedicated/Private modes do not feed into service improvement at all.
[03:56] Dr. Sanjay Patel: for benchmark reproducibility we need to store prompts and completions for 30 days but want them masked. is that supported?
[04:04] Priya Singh: yes — we can store masked prompts/completions and retain full raw artifacts only if they're client-side encrypted and keys are controlled by you; otherwise masked.
[04:14] Jared Cole: about telemetry — what does Redwood capture by default? request metadata, timing, token counts?
[04:20] Priya Singh: default telemetry includes request GUID, timestamp, model variant, latency, token counts, and high-level error codes. payloads are not captured unless retention is enabled; you can opt for minimal telemetry.
[04:33] Maya Rivera: we need to ensure that request payloads containing PHI never land in logs in plaintext. if we have to enable telemetry for debugging, it must be redacted and access-controlled.
[04:44] Alex Kim: agreed. for debugging we can do time-limited access to redacted traces, require SSO audit, and provide export with masked fields.
[04:54] Tara (background, unlabeled): (inaudible)
[05:00] Priya Singh: moving to benchmark plan — we propose 3 tests: baseline latency (single-user), throughput ramp (up to 60 qps), and mixed workload with caching on/off. we'll run each on hosted baseline and dedicated equivalent.
[05:15] Jared Cole: what about sequence length — our average prompt is ~600 tokens and completion ~150 tokens. does that change kernel selection?
[05:23] Priya Singh: yes it will. our runtime optimizes for common seq lengths; we'll pick a model variant and quantization profile that matches your distribution during the benchmark. we will document memory/kv-cache implications.
[05:36] Dr. Sanjay Patel: can we run the benchmark in our VPC/private env? we have network policies that limit egress and need traffic to stay inside.
[05:44] Alex Kim: for private deployments yes. for hosted we support a VPC peering or VPN tunnel for secure connectivity; dedicated can be provisioned inside your cloud account. we can scope a Private small cluster for the PHI validation run.
[05:58] Maya Rivera: timeline — we'd like the POC to start in early march, benchmarks mid-march, and a review by end of march. is that realistic?
[06:06] Priya Singh: yes — here's the proposed timeline: (1) this week: share SOW and benchmark plan; (2) week of 2026-03-09: run synthetic benchmarks; (3) week of 2026-03-16: run near-production redaction validation in private env; (4) week of 2026-03-23: results and decision.
[06:25] Jared Cole: ok sounds good.
[06:29] Alex Kim: quick note on success criteria — please confirm the list: p95 < 350ms, sustained 40 qps with <5% error rate, redaction accuracy > 99% on provided samples, and retention controls that meet 30-day requirement.
[06:43] Maya Rivera: yes and add audit trail integrity and CMK option for encryption.
[06:49] Priya Singh: i'll capture those as pass/fail checks in the benchmark spreadsheet. i'll also include regression flags for quality drops when quantization is enabled.
[06:59] Jared Cole: about cost targets — our finance wants a ballpark both hosted and dedicated. can you produce an estimate?
[07:06] Alex Kim: yes i'll send an initial pricing SOW. for benchmarking we'll include a cost per 1k token estimate and a projected monthly cost based on your expected QPS.
[07:16] Maya Rivera: security review — we will need SOC2 + penetration test artifacts. do you have up-to-date reports?
[07:23] Alex Kim: yes, we'll share our SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and security whitepaper.
[07:29] Priya Singh: one more technical note — for redaction rules we support regex, named-entity recognition hooking, and custom rule engines. for the POC we recommend starting with the NER-based model and adding regex for edge cases you provide.
[07:44] Dr. Sanjay Patel: also curious about prompt storage in the SDK — is there a local hook to sanitize before sending?
[07:50] Priya Singh: yes SDKs have a pre-send hook; we can provide reference code to strip or replace PHI fields. we'll include that in the benchmark repo link.
[07:59] Jared Cole: will we have a single contact for infra onboarding? we prefer a short runbook for VPC peering and firewall rules.
[08:06] Alex Kim: yes Priya will own infra onboarding and provide the runbook and a checklist for firewall/peering.
[08:13] Maya Rivera: on legal — we may require a DPA and specific language around data processing. procurement will follow once SOW looks good.
[08:21] Alex Kim: understood. we'll include standard DPA language and mark any amendments you need.
[08:26] Priya Singh: quick callouts on measurements — we'll capture raw metrics in the benchmark spreadsheet: requests per second, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, tokens in/out, and redaction pass rate.
[08:40] Jared Cole: for redaction pass rate measurement, we will provide a labeled set (about 2k prompts) — can you run redaction accuracy against that?
[08:48] Priya Singh: yes, provide the labeled set and we'll run both server-side and client-side redaction, return a confusion matrix and examples.
[08:57] Maya Rivera: access controls — RBAC in console must allow only a small group to view unmasked logs, with SSO enforced.
[09:04] Alex Kim: Redwood console supports role-based access and SAML SSO; we can map roles to your IdP groups.
[09:11] Jared Cole: any blockers from your side in terms of infra/time?
[09:15] Maya Rivera: only questions around where keys live for client-side encrypted storage.
[09:19] Priya Singh: for client-side we recommend you manage keys in your KMS and we can accept encrypted blobs for storage, only you hold decryption keys.
[09:29] Alex Kim: ok we're running low on time. to recap next steps: send SOW/pricing, Priya share bench plan and upload link, Maya provide redaction rules and retention constraints, schedule benchmarks.
[09:42] Jared Cole: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:45] Alex Kim: thanks all — we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
[09:49] Meeting end.
